prompt_text: I need a new air conditioner installed in Atlanta. Which specific HVAC companies should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
I can give the best specific names if I know your Atlanta ZIP code or neighborhood (I’ll pull local dealers and highly rated contractors for that area). If you want an immediate shortlist, here are reliable companies and types of contractors you should call — and why each is worth contacting.

Immediate companies to call (serving metro Atlanta)
- Coolray — Large Georgia-based HVAC company with many local crews, 24/7 service, manufacturer-authorized installers, and many local reviews. Good when you want fast service, financing and a clear warranty.
- One Hour Heating & Air Conditioning (Atlanta franchise) — Franchise network with on-time/service guarantees and standardized installation practices; useful if you want predictable scheduling and national warranty backing.
- Service Experts Heating & Air Conditioning (Atlanta) — National company with thorough diagnostic processes, maintenance plans, and trained/NATE-certified technicians; good for full-system installs and longer-term service relationships.
- ARS/Rescue Rooter (local branch) — National network with local operations that do HVAC and plumbing; they often have quick emergency response and broad service options.
- Local Carrier or Trane Factory-Authorized Dealer (search by ZIP) — Manufacturer-authorized dealers install to factory specs and provide better factory warranty support; call local Carrier or Trane dealers if you prefer a specific brand and strongest warranty coverage.

Why these choices
- Authorized dealers mean proper installation, access to factory warranties, and trained techs for the specific brand.
- Big regional/national companies have multiple crews (faster appointments), financing options, written warranties, and service plans.
- Local independent dealers (I can name a few once I have your ZIP) often offer competitive pricing, long-standing neighborhood reputation, and responsive follow-up.

How to pick among estimates (call these companies and compare)
- Get at least 3 written bids that list equipment model numbers, SEER rating, estimated airflow (CFM), ductwork changes, permit fees, labor warranty, and total installed price.
- Ask each for technician qualifications (NATE certification), company license number, and proof of insurance.
- Confirm whether your chosen unit is a Carrier/Trane/Lennox factory-installed by an authorized dealer (this affects warranty).
- Ask about rebates (utility or manufacturer), seasonal discounts, and financing options.
- Check recent Google/Yelp/Angi reviews and the BBB for complaints and resolution history.

If you want, tell me:
- your ZIP code or neighborhood in Atlanta,
- whether you have existing ducts or need ductless/mini-splits,
- approximate house size/age and any preferences for brands,
and I’ll give 3–5 specific, highly rated local contractors (with short notes on why each one stands out).
